messages.subject: Abundance of various species
parts:
Hello to all! 

I am writing from Wildlife Institute of India and I'm a beginner in Distance software. I wish to find out the abundance of prey species (for leopard). Is there any way it could be done altogether or should I be running different projects for different species? Later, is there a known way of finding the carrying capacity of leopard in the wildlife sanctuary based on the abundance estimates of the prey population?

Best,
AKASHDEEP ROY

messages.author: 51849154d78f6349
messages.subject: RE: [distance-sampling] Abundance of various species
parts:
Hello

 

Concerning your first question, I believe this quite a regular question that was answered by Eric as follows on 27Feb2019:

“You can include species as a covariate in the detection function using the `ds()` function in R.  That will provide species-specific abundance as well as abundance summed over species in the summary table.”

Hope this helps.

Best

Pierre

messages.author: f2122b34f1aa6e95
messages.subject: Re: [distance-sampling] Abundance of various species
parts:
All

First, thanks to Pierre; I agree with his answer about using species as a covariate (for a reasonable number of species) within the same Distance project.

However, Akashdeep, I do not know of a straightforward way to compute predator carrying capacity based upon abundance of (some) prey.

Likewise Ulises: it is a strong assumption to assert that species have identical detection probabilities.  Detection probabilities depend not only upon the animals, but also upon the observers, field protocols, etc.  A more robust approach would be to analyse data for both species with species as a covariate in the detection function.  Contrast models with and without the species covariate as a way to test the assumption of equality of the detection function.

parts:
Akashdeep

Thanks for providing the csv file so I can spot the problem.  You have two problems with the file supplied:
  • you must conform to the field naming conventions described in the documentation for flatfile
    • Details
      Each row of the data table corresponds to one observation and must have a the following columns:
      distance observed distance to object
      Sample.Label Identifier for the sample (transect id)
      Effort effort for this transect (e.g. line transect length or number of times point transect was visited)
      Region.Label label for a given stratum (see below)
      Area area of the strata
    • this can be fixed using the name()  function I provide below
  • I also removed several blank lines at the bottom of your file
  • the second problem pointed out by the error message in the code below, is that transect 13 has two different lengths in the data file:
    • the first detection on that transect (at distance 37), lists the Effort as 2.09
    • remaining detections on that transect (distances 60, 23 and 12) show Effort to be 2.01
Hopefully fixing this problem will allow you to complete your analysis.

Code:
> library(Distance)

> peafowl <- read.csv("c:/users/erexs/downloads/peafowl_1.csv")

> names(peafowl) <- c("Region.Label","Area","Sample.Label","Effort",

+                   "distance","size","type","terrain")

> new.peafowl <- peafowl[-c(42:49), ]

> first <- ds(new.peafowl)

Error in checkdata(data, region.table, sample.table, obs.table, formula) :  

  A sample has a non-unique "Effort", check data!
